mutations.rationale: The other half of D14: the re-armed handoff must carry the LINKED run's id so its outbox dedupe key matches whatever the other runtime enqueued. Publishing the derived id would name a run that does not exist, turning a scheduler-visible fault into a permanent worker failure.

Inverts fairness to least-overdue-first. The two-pass split guarantees only AGGREGATE progress; PER-REPORT progress comes from most-overdue-first ordering. Reversed, a carried-over report is displaced by every newer arrival and starves indefinitely — the same starvation as the budget-refill bug, one level up, and the reason the bound must depend on population rather than arrival rate.

Restores the unconditional overwrite. The loop polls far more often than any schedule is due, so a window that never ran the producer cleared a live degraded reason on the very next poll — making a permanent fault visible for one poll interval and invisible to any realistic scrape. This is what made the whole per-report degraded fix unobservable in practice, so the fix and its signal must be mutated separately. Must be proved through the loop's exported metric, not the engine's returned ScheduleResult: a test that only inspects Step's return never reaches Loop.record.

Removes the tie-break, leaving the order stable rather than total. Ties are the common case, not an edge case — reports sharing a cron and last run all have the same due instant. Without the tie-break the order depends on arrival sequence, and two schedulers do NOT read the same rows because SKIP LOCKED gives each a different subset, so replica agreement would rest on a clause in another function.

Claims every window evaluated the schedule, including duplicate claims and cold-start baselines that never ran the producer. That reintroduces the M6 defect from the engine side rather than the loop side: a window with no verdict would assert one, clearing a live degraded reason. The replacement deliberately keeps `evaluated` referenced: an earlier version used `if true`, which made the variable unused and killed the mutation with a COMPILE error, so no test ran and the kill was not evidence about any assertion. Only reachable where an occurrence IS due but the producer does not run - a cold-start baseline or a duplicate claim - so a test exercising ordinary due/not-due windows cannot detect it.

Lets ErrScheduledReportUndeliverable propagate out of Produce, which is the H1 regression itself: the engine rolls the transaction back, so ONE tenant's stranded run discards every other tenant's freshly materialized run and handoff — on every tick, permanently, because last_run_at never advances while a run is pending. This pins the ISOLATION half; M26 pins detection. Python is strictly more available here, dispatching each row independently and bypassing the outbox entirely.
